subject: Post-call: sizing token slab + continuous-batching assumptions
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@finityhealth.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@finityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: sizing token slab + continuous-batching assumptions

Hi Asha / Rajiv — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can size a short PoC: 

What we heard (high level)
- Workload: user chat + scheduled summarization jobs. Mix is ~70% chat (avg prompt 110 tokens, avg generation 420 tokens) and 30% nightly summarization (avg prompt 900 tokens, generation 1,200 tokens).
- Expected ramp: 100k tokens/day immediate, scale to ~15M tokens/day in 6–9 months if retention/feature adoption goes well.
- Latency target: 90th percentile < 750ms for chat interactive flows; background jobs can be >2s.
- Sticky sessions: chat sessions have strong temporal locality (many consecutive tokens per session — KV cache reuse is important).

Key cost / pricing topics to confirm
- Target unit economics: Finity asked for a target near $0.80 / 1M tokens as a starting negotiation point, but open to tradeoffs for latency/SLA.
- Budget band: initial monthly budget band mentioned $10k–$40k; want clarification if PoC spend sits inside first band.

Batching & concurrency assumptions we discussed
- Continuous batching expected: high steady-state chat traffic during business hours with short bursts; this favors small batch windows (~25–75ms) to keep p50 low while still batching.
- Concurrency: estimate 80–120 concurrent chat sessions at peak east-coast working hours, with an average of 3 in-flight generation requests per user.
- KV cache hit assumptions: chat stickiness implies KV cache hit rate ~65–80% which materially reduces per-token compute.

Next steps (asks from Finity -> Redwood)
1) Finity: share 48–72h anonymized sample traffic (CSV or gz) showing prompt+generation token counts by timestamp (we attached a small sample format).
2) Redwood: provide a 2-week PoC plan with an estimate of expected $/1M tokens under two profiles: "latency-optimized" and "cost-optimized". We'll include recommended batching window, expected batch sizes, and a baseline concurrency config.
3) Both: agree on a handful (3) of eval prompts to monitor quality regressions during quantization/throughput tuning.

I've attached a sample workload CSV format and a rough pricing estimate we discussed. Happy to set a short call this week to align on what sample data to send.

Best,
Jonas
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: workload_samples.csv (sample), redwood-pricing-estimate-v1.pdf (rough banding)

Subject: Re: Post-call: sizing token slab + continuous-batching assumptions

Thanks Jonas — helpful summary. Two clarifications from our side: 

1) The 15M/day is gross tokens (prompt + gen). For budgeting we treat 1M tokens ~= prompt+response combined.
2) Our sample traffic will include per-request session_id, prompt_tokens, generated_tokens, timestamp. We'll strip PII before sending.

A couple of quick asks:
- Can you give a back-of-envelope estimate for $/1M tokens in the latency-optimized vs cost-optimized profiles? Even a range helps us validate the budget band.
- For the PoC, can we limit to east-coast region first? We want to test under our primary production load.

We'll aim to send a 72h export by Thu EOD.

— Asha
Senior PM, Platform
Finity Health
asha@finityhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: sizing token slab + continuous-batching assumptions

Hi Asha — quick back-of-envelope pricing ranges so you have something to validate the budget against before the PoC traffic arrives. These are preliminary; we'll refine with the real sample. Assumptions: modern open LLM, quantized runtime, continuous batching with prefix caching 

- Latency-optimized profile (batch window ~25ms, low quant: higher compute): $1.20–$1.90 / 1M tokens
- Cost-optimized profile (batch window ~75ms, aggressive batching + higher quant): $0.55–$0.95 / 1M tokens

Tradeoffs to call out:
- If KV cache hit rate stays >=70% for chat, practical unit cost moves toward the low end of the ranges.
- Nightly summarization (long sequences) is more expensive per token due to longer generation loops and less batching efficiency for very long sequences; expect ~1.6x effective cost for those flows vs chat.

PoC plan (2 weeks) — short version:
- Phase 0 (2 days): ingest sample traffic + privacy scrub + run offline token distribution analysis.
- Phase 1 (5 business days): run mirrored traffic on Redwood Private/Dedicated testpool with 1 model variant, continuous batching enabled. Monitor latency p50/p90, batch size distribution, cache-hit curve.
- Phase 2 (remaining): cost & quality tuning, deliver a report with recommended batch window, concurrency ceiling, and an estimated blended $/1M tokens.

Operational asks for the sample export (to speed analysis)
- CSV columns: timestamp_iso, session_id, prompt_tokens, generated_tokens, route_type (chat|batch), region.
- A 2% random sample of sessions with full prompt text (redacted) for eval prompt selection.

If this looks good I'll draft a short SOW and a sandbox access plan for the east-coast pool.

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
